title: Maximum Pyramid Height
statement:
In UtmostLand the government wants to build the tallest pyramid it can from `N` special cuboid blocks. Every block has the same unit height, but the blocks differ in width: block `i` has width `w[i]`.

The pyramid is built from levels stacked on top of each other. Every level uses at least one block, and a block belongs to at most one level (you may leave blocks unused). The pyramid is valid when **each level, compared with the level directly below it,** has:

- strictly **fewer blocks**, and
- a strictly **smaller total width** (the sum of the widths of its blocks).

Because every block has unit height, the height of the pyramid is its number of levels. Find the maximum possible height.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `N`.
The second line contains `N` integers `w[0] ... w[N-1]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the maximum height of a valid pyramid.

examples.explanation: Use the top level {1} (width 1), the middle level {1, 2} (width 3) and the bottom level {3, 4, 5} (width 12). Each level has more blocks and more total width than the one above. Four levels would need at least 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10 blocks, but only 6 exist.
One block on top and two blocks below (total width 14 > 7) gives height 2. Height 3 would need 6 blocks.
A single block forms a one-level pyramid.

hints: Going down the pyramid the number of blocks must strictly increase, so a pyramid of height h needs at least 1 + 2 + ... + h blocks.

Widths are positive. If you sort the widths and give the smallest blocks to the top level, the next smallest to the next level and so on, does the width condition ever fail once the counts are 1, 2, 3, ...?
Build levels of size 1, 2, 3, ... from the sorted widths and stop when the remaining blocks cannot fill the next level.
